body.statement: For a directed acyclic graph that is a disjoint union of directed edges, the multivariate restricted additive-noise condition in Peters et al.'s Definition 27 specializes to the conjunction of their bivariate Condition 19 over the edges; under that condition their Theorem 28 identifies the directed acyclic graph from the observational law.

source.verbatim_statement: Definition 27 considers an additive noise model with p variables and requires, for all j in V and i in PA_j, the indicated conditional bivariate triple to satisfy Condition 19. Theorem 28 states: Then, G_0 is identifiable from the joint distribution.

attestation.note: Verified against the primary JMLR PDF, Peters et al. (2014), volume 15, pages 2024-2025 (PDF page 16), at https://jmlr.org/papers/volume15/peters14a/peters14a.pdf. In a disjoint union of directed edges, each non-source has its unique edge-parent and other blocks are independent, so Definition 27 reduces edgewise to Condition 19; Theorem 28 supplies graph identifiability under causal minimality.
